purpose: Optional curated event packs merged into the layered timeline at runtime. Packs add non-redundant bridge events without bloating the sparse roadmap base.
rules: Event ids must be globally unique across the base timeline and all packs.
Packs add overlays and bridge events without duplicating roadmap milestones already present in the base timeline.
When a pack event becomes a canonical roadmap milestone, move it to the base timeline and remove the duplicate pack entry.
Conversation archaeology must preserve provenance and distinguish user-originated material from later assistant synthesis.
Comparative research must keep dated project-side language separate from later research unlocks and comparisons.
Public-source packs must distinguish first-in-batch from first-known and must not overstate incomplete search coverage.
Approximate events use range precision and remain recovery targets until stronger dating is available.
Distinct project identity tracks retain their established canonical dates rather than being silently merged.
Later research unlocks are dated to the unlock unless a distinct earlier project-side event is independently sourced.
Body-symbol entries must distinguish biology, symbolism and historical comparison; anatomy is not proof of a theological claim.
Administrative, autobiographical and symbolic-authority language remain separate evidence classes; symbolic language does not establish civic authority.
Project-biography legal entries defer to stronger legal records and keep procedural findings inside the legal evidence layer.
Conversation promotions preserve conversation provenance and are not public first attestations without independent public sourcing.
Expression-development events should mark a change in grammar, modality, role or ethical orientation; routine repetitions belong in specialist ledgers.
Foresight entries must distinguish prediction, warning, scenario, dream or vision, retrospective correspondence and unresolved memory.
